analysis.title: US Equity Strategy: Outlook 2027: After the derating, how to invest
key_insights: The S&P 500 forward P/E fell about 20% in 2026 (17.7x from 22x at end-2025) even though 2026 EPS is on track to grow about 33%. UBS attributes the derating to AI ROI and regulatory concerns, higher yields and credit spreads, Iran-driven oil, tighter financial conditions and a drop in net buybacks.

History after big deratings is supportive. In years following a >10% fall in the SPX P/E, SPX returned a median 20% (average 17%) with few negative years, and the P/E recouped almost 30% of the prior decline. 1973-74 and 2021-22 are the exceptions.

UBS forecasts SPX EPS growth of 18% to $430 in 2027 and 14% to $490 in 2028. NVDA, MU and AVGO alone are about 45% of 2027 EPS growth. Semis and hardware are over 57% of the $600bn+ rise in SPX earnings, led by NVDA ($150bn+), MU ($90bn+) and AVGO ($30bn+).

Targets: SPX 8900 at end 2027 (about 18x 2028 EPS of $490, with little re-rating assumed) and 9600 at end 2028 (17.5x forward EPS). The 2026 target was cut to 7900. UBS says the volatile, positioning-driven backdrop makes the 2026 target harder to reach, but sees potential for a rebound into early 2027.

Midterm results add a 2028 risk. State-level data center pauses put about 30% of expected 2028 US capacity additions at risk, including 18GW in Texas. Policy details are unlikely before next year, so UBS trimmed 2028 EPS growth slightly, says risks are skewed lower, and will revisit as details emerge.

AI demand is accelerating. Annualized q/q cloud revenue growth nearly tripled to about $86bn in Q3 from about $31bn in Q1, on a roughly $540bn run rate. UBS analyst cloud estimates are about 15% above consensus for the next four quarters. Consensus has dollar growth flattening in 2H27.

UBS puts AI compute revenue potential at about $2.5tr at the midpoint in 5 years (range $1.1-3.9tr), above the $2tr low hurdle needed to earn a return on $6-8tr of cumulative 2025-30 capex. Including next-generation products raises the midpoint to about $3.3tr. The top of the hurdle likely relies on products maturing in the 2030s.

Valuation framework: NTM EPS is about 40% above its long-run trend, and since 1984 the SPX forward P/E has fallen about 4% for every 10pp of NTM EPS growth above the ~6.5% trend. That implies a 4-5% derating in 2027, but UBS expects big deratings to partly reverse and assumes the P/E holds near 18x.

The SPX P/E sits well below UBS's model-implied P/E (above 24x this year). Excluding NVDA, MU, AVGO, SNDK and AMD, the P/E has also fallen below implied after trading above it for most of 2024-25. The implied P/E would still be about 21x at end-2027 if sales CAGR halves and the CFROI premium falls by a third.

Theme 1: buy the Semis derating and the AI application layer. AI-exposed Semis trade at about 10x P/E with a P/E down about 45-57%. Buy Semis over Tech Hardware, with Software, Hyperscalers and NDX over RTY. The AI Exposed Semis basket (UBXXSEMA) is the top thematic basket.

Software is mostly the AI application layer. About 85% of its market cap is AI net beneficiaries, sales CAGR is about 20% (highest in over a decade), and P/E to sales CAGR has halved to about 1.1x, near 15-year lows. HOLT forecasts large-cap Software CFROI at a decade high of 18% in 2027.

Hyperscalers own scarce compute. A 62GW gap between chip-implied capacity and the power-constrained path by 2030 lets owners of installed capacity price to the marginal buyer. Neoclouds fund externally under tightening standards. UBS reads 2027 deployment as the signpost: the power path confirms the position, and about 50GW on the chip path breaks it.

UBS favors compute over the building shell because chips last about 6 years and need replacing, while buildings, power and cooling last about 20 years. AI preferences on REVS run Semis+Software > Hyperscalers > AI Power+Industrials.

Theme 2: Growth+CFROI at a discount should lead, with Healthcare most attractive. The CFROI spread between top and bottom quintiles is in the 99th percentile since 2004, while the P/E spread is only in the 43rd. Overweight Healthcare funded by Staples, since Healthcare trades at about 3x P/E to sales growth against over 6x for Staples.

Staples is UBS's highest conviction reversal trade. The roughly 12% rally in the last month is read as an unwind of a consensus funding trade and flight to safety, not better fundamentals. Staples' earnings, valuation and expected sales growth scores are near the bottom 5% of their three-year histories.

Energy exposure is reduced after a roughly 40% YTD rally. It screens rich versus fundamentals, and UBS's baseline is eventual Iran de-escalation and lower oil. Higher energy prices than recent peaks would hurt demand.

Theme 3: the expansion is intact, so fade the slowdown with cyclicals over bond proxies. Financials are the top cyclical on supportive valuations and solid earnings, and clarity on stress capital buffer rules could lift payouts more than consensus expects. Industrials and Materials are preferred over Discretionary. Staples, Utilities and REITs stay funding sources.

Theme 4: rates stay high for longer. UBS economists expect two more Fed hikes. AI-related debt issuance competes with government borrowing, pressuring weaker borrowers. UBS is underweight the High Leverage basket (UBEQHLEV) and favors Real Rates Higher (UBXXRRHI) over Rate Cut Winners (UBXXCUT).

Net buybacks are expected to rebound. SPX quarterly net buybacks fell about $120bn from Q1 to Q3 as hyperscalers swung from about $120bn a year of net buybacks to net issuing about $150bn annualized. Consensus cash flow points to a $200-400bn rise next year, with MU, NVDA and AVGO buybacks rising to $422bn by 2028 from $83bn in 2026.

The main risks are a slowdown in AI capex and a further yield spike. UBS also notes a possible shift in the post-election narrative: data center moratoriums could ease overspending and financing concerns even as they slow the buildout.

earnings_insights: UBS forecasts SPX 2027 EPS of $430, up 18% y/y after about 33% adjusted growth in 2026. Ex-Tech earnings are expected to grow about 9% and Tech about 30% (from above 50% in 2026).
UBS forecasts SPX 2028 EPS of $490, about 14% y/y and in line with consensus. Ex-Tech grows about 8% and Tech about 19%. The 2029 EPS assumption is $550, up 12%.

NVDA, MU and AVGO alone account for about 45% of the $600bn+ rise in SPX earnings in 2027, supported by backlogs. UBS has high conviction in 2027 earnings and lower confidence in 2028 because of data center regulatory risk.
SPX NTM earnings are set to rise 15%+ and UBS forecasts NTM EPS up 18% next year. SPX NTM EPS is about 40% above its long-run trend.
Ex-Tech earnings are underpinned by 2% US real GDP and a jump in business equipment investment fueled by AI capex. Investment ex AI is recovering from a multi-year recession.

macro_indicators.reading: Two more Fed hikes expected by UBS economists (about 2 hikes over the next 8 months)
macro_indicators.interpretation: Rates vol should fall on benign hikes. When the Fed hiked less than 100bp within a year of rate spikes, SPX rallied 18% on average the next year.
About 21% above the level at the time of writing on LTM P/E terms, in line with median returns after big deratings.
Assumes 14% EPS growth in 2028, 12% in 2029 and a 17.5x forward P/E.

macro_indicators.reading: Expansion and slowdown probabilities both just below 40%
macro_indicators.interpretation: Recovery probability has fallen and slowdown probability has risen. UBS expects market pricing to oscillate between the two regimes.
Supports about 9% ex-Tech earnings growth alongside AI-led business equipment investment.

macro_indicators.reading: Eventual lower oil futures prices in the UBS baseline, with Brent at 150 and 60 as scenario bounds
macro_indicators.interpretation: Lower oil would help consumers and energy users at the expense of the Energy sector. Escalation remains a risk.

macro_indicators.reading: Expected to remain elevated through the end of the year
macro_indicators.interpretation: Supports a higher-for-longer rates stance and the preference for baskets that do not need rate cuts.

trade_ideas.rationale: NDX forward EPS has risen about 2x more than RTY's, yet NDX P/E is back near 2022 lows. NDX has median net cash and a CFROI of about 30% against about 10% for RTY.
trade_ideas.risk: Sharply lower rates for good reasons, and AI disappointment.

trade_ideas.description: Overweight Semis over Tech Hardware (AI Exposed Semis basket UBXXSEMA)
trade_ideas.rationale: Semis' forward sales CAGR is about 32% versus 10% for Tech Hardware, with about 53% CFROI versus about 31%, and a P/E of about 10x.
trade_ideas.risk: Data center slowdown after the midterms, and negative Semis sentiment.

trade_ideas.description: Overweight Software, AI Software Pioneers basket (UBXXAISP)
trade_ideas.rationale: Software P/E to sales CAGR has halved to about 1.1x, near 15-year lows, while sales CAGR has risen to about 20%.
trade_ideas.risk: The roughly 15% of Software weight that is AI exposed or has no clear AI monetization path.

trade_ideas.description: Overweight Healthcare funded by Staples (Longevity & Wellness basket UBEQLGWL)
trade_ideas.rationale: Healthcare trades at about 3x P/E to sales growth against over 6x for Staples, and tops REVS rankings.
trade_ideas.risk: A continued defensive rally in Staples.

trade_ideas.description: Growth+CFROI at a Discount basket (UBEQHGCD) over Expensive Fundamentals basket (UBEQEXFN)
trade_ideas.rationale: 16x P/E versus 21x, with a 14% forward sales CAGR versus 5% and a 33% CFROI versus 6%.
trade_ideas.risk: Growth and CFROI rolling over, though compressed P/E spreads already discount it.

trade_ideas.description: Quality Capital Providers basket (UBEQQCAP) and US Infrastructure (UBXXINFR) over Consumer Cyclicals (UBXXCCYC)
trade_ideas.rationale: Expresses the expansion view: financials with supportive earnings and valuation, and AI-led investment over a weaker consumer.
trade_ideas.risk: Lower oil would help the consumer, and a slower 2028 buildout.

trade_ideas.description: Real Rates Higher basket (UBXXRRHI) over Rate Cut Winners (UBXXCUT), underweight High Leverage basket (UBEQHLEV)
trade_ideas.rationale: Rate Cut Winners has the weakest earnings change score of the thematic baskets, and High Leverage ranks poorly on REVS and is most exposed to high rates.

trade_ideas.description: Underweight Staples (reversal trade) and reduce Energy exposure
trade_ideas.rationale: Staples' rally is tactical, not fundamental. Energy is up about 40% YTD and screens rich versus fundamentals.
trade_ideas.risk: Oil escalation for Energy, and a continued flight to safety for Staples.

risk_factors: AI capex slowing, including from data center pauses after the midterms that put about 30% of 2028 capacity additions at risk.
A further spike in bond yields. UBS scenario 3 has a 10-year at 6.5% forcing the Fed to 5.5% and then a 2028 recession.
AI demand and capex disappointing, leading to recession and 6.5% unemployment (UBS scenario 4).
Iran escalation, with Brent at 150 adding 1.5pp to CPI and holding the Fed higher (UBS scenario 1).
Above-trend EPS growth keeps pressure on the P/E, pointing to a 4-5% derating in 2027 and 3% in 2028 on UBS's historical relationship.
AI prices could fall faster than usage rises, slowing lab revenue before enterprises adopt at scale.
Power and regulation remain binding constraints on data center buildout.
Concentration risk: NVDA, MU and AVGO account for about 45% of 2027 SPX earnings growth.
Weak equity markets could hit consumer earnings through wealth effects, and lower oil is a risk to the consumer-underweight view.
charts_described: Figure 2 shows AI cloud revenue surging on a steepening S curve while consensus expects flattening.
Figure 4 shows SPX returns have been a median 20% in years following >10% deratings.
Figure 8 shows SPX baseline versus upside and downside scenarios, including Brent at 150, Brent at 60, a 10-year at 6.5%, and AI demand and capex disappointing.
Figure 21 states SPX NTM EPS has risen to about 40% above trend and the forward P/E has fallen about 20% YTD.
Figure 23 shows S&P 500 NTM P/E below the UBS model-implied value.
Figure 62 shows power constraints could create a 62GW deployment gap by 2030.
vol_and_positioning: Rates vol jumped to fairly extreme levels in 2026 and UBS expects it to fall if the Fed hikes two more times.
The report says positioning is sharply reduced in Semis, and that the volatile backdrop is increasingly driven by positioning and technicals.

Net buybacks, a key source of equity demand, fell about $120bn from Q1 to Q3. UBS expects a $200-400bn rebound next year, with Q1 seasonally the strongest quarter and announcements picking up in the last 1-2 months.
Sentiment is a bigger overhang for Financials despite supportive earnings and valuation. Sentiment toward Semis is negative, which UBS calls a counterweight to its preference.
Staples' recent 12% rally is read as an unwind of a consensus funding trade.
geopolitical: The Iran conflict was one of the key drivers of oil, rates and equities in 2026. UBS sees eventual de-escalation as the end point, though escalation remains a risk.
US midterm election results: governor-elects supporting data center construction pauses put about 30% of expected 2028 capacity additions at risk, including 18GW in Texas.
The report cites a Democratic sweep in the midterms as the largest downside risk, since it could lead to bans and limits on new data centers.

tension_points.bull_case: Annualized q/q cloud growth nearly tripled to about $86bn, UBS cloud estimates are about 15% above consensus, and AI compute revenue potential of about $2.5tr clears the $2tr low hurdle. Consensus flattens dollar growth in 2H27, which UBS calls conservative.
tension_points.bear_case: Capex of about $1.7tr in 2029-30 needs revenue above $3tr and next-generation products to sustain. State-level data center pauses put about 30% of 2028 capacity additions at risk, and AI prices could fall faster than usage rises.
tension_points.what_invalidates: About 50GW deployed on the chip path in 2027 would break the scarcity thesis for hyperscalers. Disappointing AI demand data points through H1 2027 would move UBS toward its AI-disappoints scenario.

tension_points.bull_case: Semis P/E is near 10x and the rest of SPX trades below the model-implied P/E. After >10% deratings the P/E has recouped about 30% of the decline the next year.
tension_points.bear_case: NTM EPS is about 40% above trend, and above-trend growth historically costs about 4% of P/E per 10pp of excess growth, pointing to a 4-5% derating in 2027.
tension_points.what_invalidates: A rate spike would push the P/E lower, and a rerating needs confidence that AI capex is durable and yields stay contained.

tension_points.bull_case: Rates vol should fall if the Fed hikes twice as UBS expects, and SPX rallied 18% on average the following year when the Fed hiked less than 100bp after rate spikes. AI-led growth extends the expansion.
tension_points.bear_case: Yields stay elevated and AI debt issuance competes with government borrowing, pressuring weak borrowers. The 10-year at 6.5% scenario forces the Fed to 5.5% and leads to a 2028 recession.
tension_points.what_invalidates: A further yield spike would undermine the cyclicals-over-bond-proxies call.

tension_points.bull_case: The OECD CLI is in expansion, AI-led business equipment spending surges in 2027, and cyclicals have round-tripped despite a still-high ISM manufacturing reading.
tension_points.bear_case: Expansion and slowdown probabilities are each just below 40%, and a slower AI buildout in 2028 plus the yield spike are risks to the stance.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Incoming macro data showing the backdrop has firmly shifted into slowdown would undermine the stance.
